subject: ALLOCATE statement
notes: NOT-IMPLEMENTED -> CONFORMS (kb/Work PB153, landed 2026-09-02). The restricted data-pointer now EXISTS as a model value: the grammar's dataPointerUsage parses `USAGE POINTER TO type-name-1` (SS13.18.60.2 general format, verified against the printed page - PDF p.533), PicInfo.RestrictedTypeName carries it, and StrongTypeModel.PointerRestriction reads it. SR4 is screened in BOTH ALLOCATE forms: the based form rejects a restricted RETURNING whose data-name-1 is not a strongly-typed group of that type, and the CHARACTERS form rejects a restricted RETURNING outright, since Format 1 specifies no data-name-1 to supply the type. SS13.18.60.3 SR18 is enforced with it ('If type-name-1 is specified, the TYPEDEF clause shall be specified for the subject of the entry'), so the only legal declaration shape - a GROUP strong typedef, a TYPEDEF'd pointer entry, and a TYPE item of it - is the one the positive golden uses. The old code-location pointed at the grammar because the tail did not parse; it is now the binder, where the rule lives.
